content: The WASH FIT process involves visits that are essential for collecting data and evaluating the implementation of the WASH FIT framework, as demonstrated in the Liberia case study. WASH FIT training materials are available online in English, French, and Russian. These modules serve as a guide and should be adapted to the local context, such as replacing photos with regionally relevant examples and aligning technical guidance with local standards. The training covers areas like water, sanitation, environmental cleaning, and healthcare waste management. Resources for conducting training, including sample agendas, evaluation sheets, and preand post-test quizzes, are also provided. The WASH FIT application enables facility teams to efficiently track and follow up on actions, while also allowing governments and partners to provide real-time support. Additionally, it facilitates the sharing of strategies to overcome challenges and encourages friendly competition among facilities. It provides an evidence-based approach for investment strategies aimed at efficiency, equity, and sustainability. The FACE Tool (Facility Evaluation Tool) is a mobile data collection tool designed for baseline assessments, monitoring, evaluation, advocacy, and project design in WASH services within schools and primary healthcare facilities. It uses JMP-recommended service ladders and indicators and is applicable in both humanitarian and development settings. The tool integrates health authorities into planning and survey teams and has been used in countries such as Bangladesh, Guinea, and South Sudan. The WASH Con tool provides a comprehensive overview of WASH conditions, infrastructure, and resources in healthcare facilities. It aligns with JMP indicators and is available as a mobile tool with automated dashboards and reports. The data collected can inform programmatic activities and advocacy efforts. The Clean Clinic Approach (CCA) is an incremental improvement tool that encourages ministries of health and healthcare facilities to establish or update WASH and infection prevention standards. It motivates progress through public accountability systems, such as annual facility certifications and rewards, and integrates WASH activities into broader quality-of-care efforts. The WASH & CLEAN Toolkit supports internal audits and research studies on hygiene in maternity wards. It enables healthcare facilities to assess hygiene conditions, identify priority areas, and develop interventions. The toolkit has been used in countries like India, Malawi, and Tanzania. The TEACH-CLEAN package provides participatory training in infection prevention and environmental hygiene, tailored for low-literate cleaning staff in maternity units but applicable to wider facility staff. It includes seven modules on essential topics like hand hygiene and waste handling, along with a Clean Box containing resources for each topic. The package has been implemented in countries such as The Gambia, India, and Cameroon. These tools and resources collectively aim to improve water, sanitation, and hygiene in healthcare facilities, contributing to better quality of care and infection prevention. They are designed to be adaptable to local contexts and support sustainable improvements in healthcare settings worldwide.
